chapter_note: This chapter is overwhelmingly cosmological-architectonic teaching (mixture of Light/Darkness; ordering of garments/firmaments; artisan metaphors for the Living Spirit/Father of Life; final separation). The only clear later layer is a brief dialogue-attribution frame at the start of ¶1, which must be stripped. The extended carpenter/architect metaphors (¶3–¶4) remain within cosmos→cosmos exposition (no institutional/NT anchoring), though they are rhetorically elaborated and could be a secondary expansion within the teaching tradition.

paragraphs.core_text: At the time when the F[ir]st [Man ...] he gave the leadership to his five [sons ... the] Living Spirit and the Mother of Life [...] as the entire ruling-power is entwined and crucified [...] they were poured out and mixed with each other, the light with the darkness and the darkness with the light.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue-attribution frame formula: "[Once again] the enlightener [speaks]:" (hagiographic compilation frame).
paragraphs.temporal_note: The opening speaker-attribution is a late compiling frame; the remainder is impersonal cosmological mechanics (mixture/crucifixion/entangling of powers) consistent with the older substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: At that time the Living Spirit called one of his sons, one rich with power. He gave to him the leadership of the garments. Now, he himself [...] of [...] he hung them and set them up [...] of the Father of Life [...] he set up all things [...] he opened [...] ten firmaments [...] the wheel of the stars [...] them and the [...].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic cosmological construction account (sons, garments, ten firmaments, wheel of the stars) in expository voice; no citation, exhortation, or institutional pointing.

paragraphs.core_text: The Living Spirit is like this: Just as [...] and an architect who might build a dwelling for the king, and divide it up into separate houses and [separate ...] everything that is required for beauty [...] and he cleans them. And also the stones [...] them for beauty and loveliness, and he arranges them and makes them so that should the king come and inhabit that palace, he might glorify him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Didactic artisan simile used to explain a cosmic function (Living Spirit as world-builder preparing a palace for a king). Despite worldly imagery, it does not anchor to contemporary institutions and stays within the cosmic analogy.

paragraphs.core_text: Furthermore, the Father of Life resembles a wise and skilled carpenter [...] before it was worked [...] before it was established and made beautiful and [...] carpenter [...] works in it, but [...] in him in his [...] in his understanding, and he brings the saw and the adze, and cuts it into separate pieces [...] it and he pulls the [...] it with the plane and he smooths it. He shall make many [...] wooden implements, arranging them shape by shape; he cuts and produces wooden implements from it, wooden implements of different kinds, (such as) dishes, bowls. This wood, that [...] since previously it had not been worked before it was sealed by [the ski]ll and wisdom of this dextrous carpenter. He cut it up into different sorts of implements useful to his master.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continuation of the craft-metaphor sequence (carpenter/tools/shaping) functioning as cosmological explanation by analogy; no explicit editorial seam into church practice or present-day polemic.

paragraphs.core_text: So is it also with the Father of Life. In his wisdom he has [...] in limbs [...] palace [...] in it or in a [...] useful [...] the ships of light [...] all the other works [...] in the [...] so that when the great king comes, he who is the Third Ambassador, who [...] he might dwell in this universe [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Returns explicitly to internal cosmological beings and structures (Father of Life; ships of light; Third Ambassador) and reads as the doctrinal referent of the preceding metaphors.

paragraphs.core_text: ... live. The light, however, that is in it [...] wise, and he takes it up to the land; but the waste and the darkness will be gathered and thrown down to the abyss.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic sorting/separation mechanism (light raised; waste/darkness cast to abyss) in impersonal process language; no institutional or NT overlay markers.
